segments.text: Job continued his discourse:
“As surely as God lives, who has deprived me of justice— the Almighty, who has embittered my soul—
segments.speaker: Job

segments.text: as long as my breath is still within me and the breath of God remains in my nostrils,
segments.speaker: Job

segments.text: my lips will not speak wickedness, and my tongue will not utter deceit.
segments.speaker: Job

segments.text: I will never say that you are right; I will maintain my integrity until I die.
segments.speaker: Job

segments.text: I will cling to my righteousness and never let go. As long as I live, my conscience will not accuse me.
segments.speaker: Job

segments.text: May my enemy be like the wicked and my opponent like the unjust.
segments.speaker: Job

segments.text: For what is the hope of the godless when he is cut off, when God takes away his life?
segments.speaker: Job

segments.text: Will God hear his cry when distress comes upon him?
segments.speaker: Job

segments.text: Will he delight in the Almighty? Will he call upon God at all times?
segments.speaker: Job

segments.text: I will instruct you in the power of God. I will not conceal the ways of the Almighty.
segments.speaker: Job

segments.text: Surely all of you have seen it for yourselves. Why then do you keep up this empty talk?
segments.speaker: Job

segments.text: This is the wicked man’s portion from God— the heritage the ruthless receive from the Almighty.
segments.speaker: Job

segments.text: Though his sons are many, they are destined for the sword; and his offspring will never have enough food.
segments.speaker: Job

segments.text: His survivors will be buried by the plague, and their widows will not weep for them.
segments.speaker: Job

segments.text: Though he heaps up silver like dust and piles up a wardrobe like clay,
segments.speaker: Job

segments.text: what he lays up, the righteous will wear, and his silver will be divided by the innocent.
segments.speaker: Job

segments.text: The house he built is like a moth’s cocoon, like a hut set up by a watchman.
segments.speaker: Job

segments.text: He lies down wealthy, but will do so no more; when he opens his eyes, all is gone.
segments.speaker: Job

segments.text: Terrors overtake him like a flood; a tempest sweeps him away in the night.
segments.speaker: Job

segments.text: The east wind carries him away, and he is gone; it sweeps him out of his place.
segments.speaker: Job

segments.text: It hurls itself against him without mercy as he flees headlong from its power.
segments.speaker: Job

segments.text: It claps its hands at him and hisses him out of his place.
segments.speaker: Job
